purpose: Numerically stress the decision-only intersection-union rule under strong dependence while keeping its proof separate from simulation.

toy_component_process.joint_rule: declare BOTH channels safe only after both component e-processes cross 20
toy_component_process.bonferroni_reporting_comparator: require both to cross 40, corresponding to alpha=.025 each

stress_grid.dependence: At each step, with shared_fraction in {0,.5,1}, both Bernoulli channels use the same uniform draw; otherwise independent uniforms.

high_precision_dependency_checks.note: The small Monte Carlo excess over .05 is sampling noise around a theoretically level-.05 component process; the simulation is not the proof.
With one unsafe channel and one strongly safe channel under perfect shared-U dependence, the false conjunctive-safe rate tracks the unsafe component's level rather than doubling.

conclusion: The simulations are consistent with the intersection-union proof and show the practical distinction: the AND decision can use alpha on both component tests without Bonferroni splitting, even under strong dependence, while two simultaneously reported numerical bounds still require a joint-coverage construction.
scope_guards: This toy simulation does not instantiate the full equal-process/planned-exposure V3 confidence sequences; it stress-tests the IUT logic with simple valid component e-processes.
Monte Carlo crossing rates are not exact error guarantees; the guarantee comes from component stopped e-validity plus union-null logic.
The no-split rule applies only to the frozen conjunctive safety decision.
